imals. It depends primarily on inter-
ference with normal nutrition of the
body. It is characterized by a def-
iciency of lime and phosphates in the
bones and, consequently, a lack of
rigidity. The deficiency may be due

in the feed, or to the failure of the
body to properly utilize the material

with nutrition and bring on "leg weak
ness." Among these may be mentioned

food, close confinement with little room

accompanied by green or other bulky
feed, and little or no animal proteins.

should be corrected. A monotonous
ration should be avoided, and if
possible, green feed or
sour milk should be provided. The
